titleEn: Dirty Hands? Splash into the Tub!

pages.text: "Hungry! Time to eat!" Pipo ran into the kitchen after playing in the potato patch. With dirty hands, he grabbed bread. "Pipo, with those hands?" Mom asked, but instead of answering, he took a big bite.
"I do not want to wash! I will eat quickly and plant more potatoes!" His big bite puffed out his cheeks. Dirt crumbled from his fingertips onto the bread. Grit crunched as he chewed.
A little later, his tummy rumbled and hurt. "Oh, my tummy..." Rubbing it with one hand, he shed a tear. Mom hurried over and examined his hands.
"Pipo, tiny wigglers you cannot see live in soil. They got on your hands and rode onto the bread!" His eyes widened. "What do I do?" "Do not worry. Come to the well with Mom."
They stood together before the water tub. "Just three steps here. One—dirty hands? Splash into the tub!" Pipo dipped both hands. Dirt loosened, clouding the water.
"Two—soap on, rub up bubbles!" Pipo rolled soap in both hands. Foam puffed up to his wrists. "Wow, like sheep's wool!" Dirty hands? Splash into the tub!

"Three—fresh water, rinse every corner!" Mom poured clean water into the tub. Pipo rinsed the backs of his hands and rubbed between his fingers. Muddy water drained away, leaving clean hands. "Goodbye, wigglers!"
Pipo shook his hands: fresh and squeaky clean. His tummy no longer hurt. Crouching by the well with hands at his chest, he said, "Now I know! Wash first, and no tummyache!"

The next day, back from the potato patch, Pipo stopped at the kitchen door and showed both hands. "Hands first before eating! One, dirty hands splash into the tub! Two, soap on and rub! Three, fresh water, every corner!" Now he did it all alone.

Mom hugged Pipo. "Our Pipo is a handwashing champion!" Clean hands made tummy and feelings comfortable. He picked up bread with clean hands. "Dirty hands? Splash into the tub! Today bread tastes twice as good!"
